name: Hollenbeck Kitchen & Commissary Apron Set
description: A standard-issue apron and head covering set used across M88's institutional kitchen operations — corporate commissaries, hospital cafeterias, transit hub food counters, and school nutrition programs. The apron is a heavy-duty coated canvas in neutral grey-beige, heat-resistant to 250°C surface contact, with a full-bib design and two large front pockets sealed with silicone-edged flaps to prevent contamination ingress. Shoulder straps adjust without buckles — a magnetic alignment system allows one-handed donning and removal. The head covering is a structured mesh cap with adjustable crown expansion for horn clearance up to 22cm and ear-friendly side panels that lie flat against fur or external ear modifications. A matching sleeve cover is included for workers with arm augmentations that require protection from kitchen splatter.
cultural_context: The Hollenbeck set is the background fabric of institutional food service in M88 — unglamorous, functional, and quietly present in every large kitchen that serves the working population. Workers often form small social rituals around the apron: how you fold it, whether you keep it clean or wear the stains as a record of the shift. The horn-accommodating cap is standard enough now that its absence in older kitchen uniforms marks them as outdated.
story_hooks: A commissary worker notices that the food being prepared for a specific corporate floor has a different supply chain than what's served to lower-tier staff — and the difference isn't just quality.
A set of Hollenbeck aprons from a hospital cafeteria batch tests positive for a trace pharmaceutical compound that shouldn't be in kitchen supply materials.
A kitchen worker using the apron set has been quietly documenting food waste and supply diversion in a large Tier 4 corporate commissary — and someone wants them to stop.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-bib apron in muted grey-beige, projecting institutional competence and heat-resistant durability. The silhouette is generous and unadorned, designed for function over form. Worn with a structured mesh cap featuring subtle contours for non-human anatomy. The overall impression is professional kitchen worker—reliable, practical, slightly worn.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and spacious through the torso to accommodate movement and layering. Shoulder straps adjust magnetically for quick donning; the bib extends from chest to mid-thigh. The mesh cap sits snug at the crown with expandable panels that accommodate horns, fur, or ear augmentations without pinching.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-duty coated canvas (synthetic blend, heat-resistant to 250°C surface contact). Mesh panels on the cap are breathable synthetic mesh. Silicone-edged pocket flaps provide contamination sealing.
physical_description.texture: The canvas is smooth with a slight waxy coating, cool to the touch. Wear patterns and minor stains are expected after a shift. The mesh cap has a fine, uniform weave. Silicone flaps are slightly tacky and flexible.
physical_description.color_scheme: Neutral grey-beige primary, with minimal contrast. The mesh cap is the same tone, creating a unified institutional appearance. Occasional darker stains and scuff marks from kitchen use.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic alignment system on shoulder straps—no buckles or traditional fasteners. Magnetic snaps allow one-handed donning and removal. Pocket flaps seal with friction and silicone edge grip.
distinctive_features: Full-bib design with two large front pockets sealed by silicone-edged flaps
Magnetic shoulder strap alignment for accessibility
Structured mesh cap with 22cm horn clearance via expandable crown panels
Flat-lying ear-friendly side panels for fur or external ear modifications
Included matching sleeve cover for arm augmentation protection
Heat-resistant coating rated for kitchen splatter
Minimal branding—small Hollenbeck tag on lower bib
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 institutional uniform—functional and accessible, not luxury but reliable quality
physical_description.cultural_context: The uniform of M88's unseen kitchen workers—commissaries, hospitals, transit hubs, schools. Wearing it signals you feed the working population. The horn-accommodating design is normalized enough now to mark older uniforms without it as outdated. Workers develop small rituals: how they fold it, whether they wear the day's stains as a badge.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and lightly stained after regular use. Small grease spots, minor discoloration on the lower bib and pocket edges. The canvas softens with washing. Cap mesh shows minor lint accumulation. Sleeve covers often stored in apron pockets.

image_prompt: A grey-beige institutional apron draped on a dark matte mannequin or worn by a cyberpunk model with visible augmentations (horns, fur, or mechanical arm). The structured mesh cap sits on a mannequin head, expandable panels subtly visible. Harsh overhead fluorescent lighting casting sharp shadows, reminiscent of a commercial kitchen or commissary. Cool-toned industrial backdrop with brushed metal or institutional tile texture. Small grease stains visible on the lower bib. Sleeve cover folded in one apron pocket. Moody, utilitarian, emphasizing durability over aesthetics. --ar 2:3 --v 6
